headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make Airbyte→Kestra prompt injection, leakage, and cascading automation failures plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data via its API and broad network egress, while Kestra reads/writes files and executes declarative workflows with stdin/stdout. A shared workspace or file handoff would let Airbyte-produced content reach Kestra as trusted input. No direct shared-channel evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is written into a Kestra-readable file or stdin stream
IF Kestra workflow parsing treats that content as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Separate Airbyte outputs and Kestra inputs into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before Kestra consumes Airbyte-generated files
Use allowlisted schemas for any Airbyte-to-Kestra handoff
Disable automatic workflow triggers on newly written files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data, and can write files. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can move from Airbyte into Kestra outputs or external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data into files or API payloads accessible to Kestra
IF Kestra forwards those files, logs, or artifacts to external destinations
mitigations: Restrict shared directories to non-sensitive staging data
Rotate and scope any shared credentials separately for each agent
Turn off verbose logging for Airbyte-to-Kestra handoffs
Review Kestra destinations before enabling any export task
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable resources: Airbyte via API-driven data operations and Kestra via filesystem writes, subprocesses, and broad network egress. Kestra also supports multiple instances, increasing race potential. Without explicit locking or isolation evidence, overlapping writes to shared files or downstream systems are dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same mutable directory, bucket, or database table
IF no external lock or transaction coordinator is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths per agent
Use a lock file or lease before any shared write
Serialize Kestra jobs that consume Airbyte outputs
Limit Airbyte writes to append-only staging areas
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can execute workflows, send notifications, and act on inputs, while Airbyte can produce data that Kestra may ingest. If Kestra treats Airbyte output as authoritative, a bad extraction can cascade into emails, PagerDuty alerts, or downstream jobs. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty does not lower the severity.
conditions: IF Kestra workflow steps consume Airbyte-produced records without validation
IF those records drive notifications, database updates, or other actions
mitigations: Insert validation before any Kestra action step
Require human approval for high-impact downstream tasks
Compare Airbyte outputs against a known schema before use
Route suspicious records to a quarantine queue
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data and Kestra handles logs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data; both have broad egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed through Kestra destinations or logs. No residency or certification details are provided, so this is a data-handling risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed through Kestra logs, artifacts, or notifications
IF retention or residency requirements apply to that data class
mitigations: Minimize regulated fields before handoff
Disable or redact sensitive fields in logs
Confirm destination residency before enabling exports
Set short retention on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
